name: Eliashib
overview: Eliashib was a male figure noted in Scripture as a descendant of Bani. He is uniquely identified by his marriage to a foreign wife, which is explicitly mentioned in Ezra 10:36. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this distinctive attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliashib means "G-d restores," reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew El, meaning God. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 10:36, emphasizes God's restorative power but was not given directly by God to the individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Eliashib was a descendant of Bani, establishing a familial connection within the post-exilic community. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented, and no other relatives or lineage details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Eliashib's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his example as a member of the returned exiles who married a foreign wife, an act that was addressed in Ezra as contrary to the covenantal purity expected of God's people. His mention highlights the challenges faced by the community in maintaining holiness and obedience to God's law during the restoration period.
